title: Module structures and functors transported by finite products
statement: Let C,D be small sites J,K and L:Sh(J,Set)⇄Sh(K,Set):V an adjunction with L preserving finite limits. Let R,S,A be sheaves of commutative rings, R on J and S,A on K. Suppose eR:|A|≅L|R| identifies the sectionwise addition and multiplication of R and A through the product comparison, and let c:A→S be a ring-sheaf map. On the module-sheaf categories [def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category], there exist functors I:Mod(R)→Mod(A) and P:Mod(S)→Mod(R), and natural isomorphisms eI:|I(-)|≅L|-| and eP:|P(-)|≅V|-|. For every M, its addition and scalar-action maps and those of I(M) have their ordinary sectionwise values, and their images under L agree through the binary-product comparison, eR and eI. For every H, its addition and scalar-action maps and those of P(H) have their ordinary sectionwise values. Addition is transported through V and eP. There is a map k:|R|×|P(H)|→V(|S|×|H|) whose projections are fst followed by the adjunct of eR⁻¹;c and snd followed by eP, and the scalar action of P(H) followed by eP equals k followed by V of the scalar action of H. No module hom-set equivalence or tensor adjunction is asserted.

proof.text: Construct the internal commutative group object of a module sheaf using its actual sectionwise zero, addition and negation. Give each finite-product-preserving functor the braided monoidal structure from chosen products. Apply Functor.mapCommGrp and evaluate its group diagrams on sections to obtain the transported sectionwise additive groups. The right adjoint preserves limits by Adjunction.rightAdjoint_preservesLimits.

Construct the actual sectionwise ring monoid and module action. Use the proved source-library Functor.modObjObj and Mod.scalarRestriction to transport the multiplicative module laws. Prove the two distributivity diagrams directly by mapping their source diagrams, using naturality of the product comparison and its projection equations. Evaluate the diagrams on sections, and deduce the zero laws by additive cancellation.

Use the sectionwise module structures to construct a PresheafOfModules, with restriction maps linear by naturality of the transported action and addition. Its underlying set presheaf is the already existing image sheaf, so it is a sheaf. Map module homomorphisms by the functor, prove linearity from the mapped operation diagrams, and obtain the module-sheaf functor with the identity underlying natural isomorphism.

Identify the supplied addition and multiplication maps with the actual sectionwise operations by extensionality. Convert their binary-product comparison equations into monoidal equations. Multiplication compatibility of the ring isomorphism identifies the transported monoid structure with the ordinary ring monoid by MonObj.ext, and hence forces unit compatibility. Apply the preceding construction to L and this ring isomorphism to obtain I.

For P, take the adjunct d of eR inverse followed by the given ring-sheaf map c. Compute mates of a binary-operation diagram by testing its two product projections, and the mate of a constant diagram by terminal uniqueness. The inverse ring comparison and c preserve addition, multiplication and one, so these mate formulas prove the required operation equations for d. Apply the same explicit module-sheaf construction to V and d.

Relate the chosen categorical binary products to the cartesian monoidal products by the unique map with the same two projections. Its naturality and its compatibility with functor product comparisons prove the two addition equations and the scalar equation for I. For H define k as prod.map d identity followed by the inverse binary-product comparison for V. The projection equations follow from the comparison API, and the scalar equation is the definition of the transported action.
